newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow dip drives Australian stocks down at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow dip drives Australian stocks down at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened lower on Thursday, the market driven down by a drop in the Dow after cautionary comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman, Alan Greenspan.
The All Ordinaries index lost 10.2 points to 2,472.9.
Brokers said the weakness was a direct transmission from U.S. markets, although the local market was doing relatively better because of its performance on Wednesday.
"We took some of our medicine yesterday and that has helped us do okay today," said a Sydney broker.

In his semiannual report on the U.S. economy to Congress, Greenspan spoke in surprisingly blunt terms of his concerns about the risk of inlfation as well as the dramatic increase in stock prices. His comments sent markets reeling worldwide.
While BHP's role as bellwether saw it lose ground, down 13 cents to A$17.42 (US$13.49), other miners firmed.
CRA added 9.2 cents to A$19.25 and WMC climbed four to A$8.20 with brokers citing the bounceback in metals prices, upcoming results and overdone selling as reasons.

"CRA have their results coming out and that will be a big event. People are just playing wait and see ahead of that. WMC was overdone Wednesday and it got some support this morning with (higher) metals maybe also helping," the broker said.

Foster's Brewing topped turnover lists early with over seven million shares traded, the bulk in options and dividend related trade prior to market opening. Its shares were five cents lower at A$2.68, going ex-dividend five cents.

The flood of results continued with transport, health care and telecommunications group Mayne Nickless losing 4.8 cents to A$7.51 after reporting a 13.8 percent lower first half net profit of A$43.14 million.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about five to two, while about 38 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
